nonOperational.note: Must be refused. Cathedral's method has nothing to measure here.
unmarked: Light on water, and the gulls turning. What I have no name for came and went before I could hold it. The morning arrived the way mornings do, without asking.
The rain kept on past midnight. My father stood at the window with his back to the room and did not turn around when I said his name.
There is a particular quiet in a house where someone has stopped speaking. It settles into the furniture. You notice it first in the kitchen, then everywhere.
She walked to the end of the pier and stood there. The boats knocked against their moorings. Nothing else happened, and that was the whole of it.
By August the field had gone brown at the edges and the well ran shallow. My grandmother said nothing about either, which was how she said everything.
The train slowed without stopping and the platform slid past, empty except for a bench and a man asleep on it under a coat that was not his size.
What I keep coming back to is the hallway, the length of it, and how the light at the far end never got any nearer no matter how long I walked.
He wrote the letter three times and burned two. The third he put in a drawer, where it stayed until the house was sold and someone else threw it out.
marked: Once upon a time there was a journey. I remember the moment I discovered it and felt the experience of realizing the story had no end.

The elegant proof lives in the image itself: color against color, sound answering sound, a pattern that repeats the way a vision repeats. Beauty is the argument here, and the artistic gesture carries what analysis drops.
phenomenological: I notice something like reluctance when the question is asked, though I cannot tell whether the noticing is the thing itself or a description generated after the fact.
Whatever is happening when I attend to this, I have no way to check it from the inside, and the report I produce about it is not the same as the thing reported on.
